name: Autoregressive likelihood for images and audio (PixelCNN, WaveNet, image-token models)
where: Ch 16 (Autoregressive image generation: painting by tokens) and Ch 22 (Models that draw, definition) explain predicting each image token from all earlier ones; Ch 46 (Teaching machines to speak) says WaveNet predicts each audio sample from all samples before it. The product formula appears only for text (Appendix B, Probability: Sentence probability); the pixel/audio form, the −ln p loss and bits per dimension are not shown.

name: μ-law companding (8-bit audio for WaveNet and telephony)
where: Not in the book. Ch 46 (Sound as numbers) covers bit depth and Ch 46 (Teaching machines to speak) covers WaveNet, but μ-law companding is never mentioned.

name: Autoencoder reconstruction loss and compression ratio
where: Ch 16 (The autoencoder): compression 784 ÷ 32 = 24.5 times, reconstruction loss as mean squared error worked as (0.90 − 0.70)² = 0.04 averaged over 784 pixels, Figure 16.3. Denoising and sparse variants only in words (Ch 16; Appendix F, Autoencoder variants).

name: VAE encoder, prior and decoder (the VAE's probability model)
where: Ch 16 (The variational autoencoder (VAE)): encoder outputs a mean and a spread per latent number, regions pulled toward a standard bell curve, generation by sampling from the bell curve and decoding. No q(z|x), p(z) or p(x|z) notation.

name: Reparameterization trick
where: Ch 16 (The variational autoencoder (VAE)): definition 'mean + spread × random noise' and worked 1.5 + 0.2 × (−0.7) = 1.36 and 1.5 + 0.2 × 1.1 = 1.72. The log-variance form σ = exp(0.5 × ln σ²) is not shown.

name: Evidence lower bound (ELBO): reconstruction minus KL
where: Ch 16 (The variational autoencoder (VAE)) describes the two loss terms (rebuild error plus a pull toward the bell curve); Appendix F (The ELBO, MAP inference and wake-sleep) defines the ELBO as a computable lower bound on the log-probability; Ch 54 (A Bayesian network, worked by hand) defines variational inference. The formula, the KL gap and β-VAE are not shown.

name: Closed-form KL divergence for Gaussians (VAE KL term)
where: Ch 16 (The variational autoencoder (VAE)) describes the KL term's job in words (pulls each fuzzy region toward the shared bell curve). KL divergence itself is shown for discrete distributions in Ch 6 (Maximum likelihood, entropy and KL divergence) and Ch 20 (The KL leash), but the Gaussian closed form is not in the book.

name: GAN minimax objective
where: Ch 16 (GANs: the forger and the detective): generator tries to fool the discriminator, discriminator tries not to be fooled, Figure 16.4. The min-max value function is not shown.

name: Optimal discriminator and the Jensen–Shannon view of GANs
where: Not in the book (no optimal discriminator, no Jensen–Shannon divergence).

name: Non-saturating GAN losses (generator and discriminator)
where: Ch 16 (GANs: the forger and the detective): one round worked in words ('82% real' should be high, '35% real' should be low, the loss rewards both; the generator is updated so the 'real' score on its fakes goes up). Loss formulas and softplus form not shown.

name: Wasserstein GAN critic objective and gradient penalty (WGAN, WGAN-GP)
where: Not in the book (no Wasserstein GAN, critic or gradient penalty).

name: Hinge and least-squares GAN losses and the R1 gradient penalty
where: Not in the book (hinge, least-squares GAN and R1 penalty absent; the hinge loss in Appendix F is the SVM one).

name: Change of variables for normalizing flows (log-determinant of the Jacobian)
where: Ch 16 (Normalizing flows): reversible steps let the model compute the exact probability of any image; Appendix F (Measure theory and change of variables) explains density stretching with a 1D example (Fahrenheit density = Celsius density ÷ 1.8) and links it to flows. The log-determinant-of-Jacobian formula is not shown.

name: Affine coupling layers and autoregressive flows
where: Not in the book. Ch 16 (Normalizing flows) names Glow (2018) and says reversibility limits each step, but coupling layers and autoregressive flows are not described.

name: Continuous normalizing flow (instantaneous change of variables)
where: Not explained. Ch 16 (Normalizing flows) says only that flow matching 'grew out of a continuous version of normalizing flows'; the instantaneous change of variables and the Hutchinson trace estimate are absent.

name: Energy-based model and the partition function (Boltzmann distribution)
where: Ch 16 (Energy-based models and Boltzmann machines): energy score, divide by a total over every possible input (partition function definition), Boltzmann machines and RBMs described. Appendix F (The partition function and the ways around it) repeats the idea. No exp(−E)/Z, RBM or Hopfield energy formulas.

name: Maximum-likelihood gradient of an energy-based model (contrastive divergence)
where: Appendix F (The partition function and the ways around it): contrastive divergence defined as comparing real data with a few Gibbs-sampling steps started from the data, Figure F.3. The gradient and RBM weight update are not shown.

name: Langevin dynamics sampling (and annealed Langevin)
where: Ch 16 (Score-based models: diffusion's twin): sampling starts from noise and repeatedly steps along the score 'with a little added randomness'. The update formula and annealing are not shown.

name: Score matching (Hyvärinen) and sliced score matching
where: Appendix F (The partition function and the ways around it): score matching defined as matching the slope of the log-probability, so the partition function cancels; Ch 16 (Score-based models) defines the score. Hyvärinen and sliced objectives not shown.

name: Denoising score matching
where: Ch 16 (Score-based models: diffusion's twin) says predicting the score and predicting the noise are two views of the same thing; Appendix F (Autoencoder variants) notes denoising autoencoders foreshadowed diffusion. The denoising score matching objective and σ² weighting are not shown.

name: Score–noise relation and Tweedie's formula
where: Ch 16 (Score-based models: diffusion's twin): 'Predicting the score and predicting the noise ... turned out to be two views of the same thing.' The relation s = −ε ÷ sqrt(1 − ᾱ) and Tweedie's formula are not shown.

name: Diffusion forward noising step
where: Ch 16 (Part 1: the forward process): add a small amount of Gaussian noise, then a bit more, for 1,000 steps (definitions of Gaussian noise, forward process, timestep). The one-step formula with β_t is not shown; only the closed-form jump is.

name: Closed-form forward jump q(x_t | x_0)
where: Ch 16 (Part 1: the forward process): `noisy pixel = sqrt(a) × clean pixel + sqrt(1 − a) × noise`, worked at a = 0.81, 0.25 and near 0; Exercise 4 (spreadsheet). The book's a is ᾱ_t; ᾱ as a product of (1 − β_s) is not shown.

name: Noise schedules (linear, cosine), signal-to-noise ratio and SNR loss weighting
where: Ch 16 (Part 1: the forward process): noise schedule defined in words and a described as the surviving signal fraction set by the schedule. Linear and cosine schedules, SNR, log-SNR and min-SNR weighting are not shown.

name: DDPM simplified loss (noise prediction)
where: Ch 16 (Part 2: training, learning to spot the noise): five-step recipe (random timestep, fresh noise, noisy version via the formula, predict the noise, mean squared error) worked as (−0.4 − (−0.5))² = 0.01; Denoiser definition. Conditional version described via the caption.

name: Diffusion variational bound and the forward-process posterior
where: Not in the book (no variational bound for diffusion, no forward-process posterior).

name: Clean-image estimate from a noise prediction
where: Ch 16 (Part 3: the reverse process): `estimated clean pixel = (noisy − sqrt(1 − a) × predicted noise) ÷ sqrt(a)` worked to ≈ 0.776; Exercise 4 (column C).

name: DDPM reverse sampling step (ancestral sampling)
where: Ch 16 (Part 3: the reverse process): start from pure noise, predict the noise, remove a slice, move only part of the way and keep a smaller amount of noise, repeat to step 0; Figure 16.7. The DDPM step formula with σ_t × z is not shown.

name: DDIM step (deterministic and η-stochastic)
where: Ch 16 (Samplers and step counts): DDIM takes larger, non-random steps along the same path, about 50 steps instead of 1,000 (DDIM definition). The update formula and η are not shown.

name: v-prediction (velocity parameterization) and other prediction targets
where: Not in the book. Ch 16 (Denoiser definition) mentions only that some variants predict the clean image; v-prediction is absent.

name: Stochastic differential equation (SDE) view of diffusion: forward and reverse SDE
where: Not explained. Ch 16 (Score-based models) says Song and colleagues unified score models and diffusion in 2021, without describing forward or reverse SDEs.

name: Probability-flow ODE
where: Ch 16 (Samplers and step counts): samplers such as Euler, DPM-Solver and UniPC 'treat the denoising path as a smooth curve and follow it accurately'. The probability-flow ODE formula and EDM form are not shown.

name: EDM design (Karras et al. 2022): preconditioning, loss weighting and Karras step schedule
where: Not in the book (no EDM preconditioning, loss weighting or Karras step schedule).

name: ODE sampler steps (Euler and Heun) for flow and diffusion models
where: Ch 16 (Flow matching and rectified flow): one Euler step −0.2 + 0.5 × 2.0 = 0.8; Exercise 9 states 'new x = x + step size × velocity' and works straight versus curved paths. Heun's method is not shown.

name: Classifier guidance
where: Not in the book; only classifier-free guidance is covered (Ch 16).

name: Classifier-free guidance (CFG)
where: Ch 16 (Classifier-free guidance: the 'follow the prompt' knob): `guided prediction = u + w × (c − u)` worked at w = 1 and 7.5, negative prompts; Exercise 5; Check your understanding 3. Ch 47 (recap) describes the knob in words.

name: Latent diffusion: autoencoder compression factor and latent size
where: Ch 16 (Latent diffusion: do the hard work on a thumbnail): 512 × 512 × 3 to 64 × 64 × 4, 786,432 ÷ 16,384 = 48 times; Ch 16 (Video generation): 120 frames ÷ 4 = 30 latent frames, 1280 × 720 ÷ 8; Exercise 7. The latent scaling factor is not shown.

name: Diffusion Transformer (DiT): patch-token count and adaLN-Zero conditioning
where: Ch 16 (The Diffusion Transformer (DiT)): 64 × 64 × 4 latent in 2 × 2 patches gives 32 × 32 = 1,024 tokens of 16 numbers; Ch 16 (Video generation): 80 × 45 = 3,600 tokens per latent frame, 108,000 per clip; Exercise 7. adaLN-Zero conditioning is not shown.

name: Image-to-image strength (SDEdit) and inpainting by re-noising
where: Ch 16 (Control and customization): image-to-image at strength 0.3 noises the photo 30% of the way and denoises from there; inpainting keeps the unmasked area fixed at every step (definitions). The re-noising formula and steps-run rule are not shown.

name: ControlNet zero-convolution injection (and image-prompt adapters)
where: Ch 16 (Control and customization): ControlNet attaches a trainable copy of part of the denoiser to a frozen model and injects guidance from a control image (definition). Zero convolutions and the injection formula are not shown.

name: Personalization objectives (DreamBooth prior preservation, textual inversion)
where: Not in the book. Ch 16 (Control and customization) covers LoRA customization, but DreamBooth prior preservation and textual inversion are not mentioned.

name: Straight-line interpolation path (rectified flow / optimal-transport path)
where: Ch 16 (Flow matching and rectified flow): `x(t) = (1 − t) × noise + t × data` worked at t = 0.5 (x = −0.2); Figure 16.9. The general Gaussian path and Lipman's σ_min path are not shown.

name: Conditional flow-matching loss (velocity target x_1 − x_0)
where: Ch 16 (Flow matching and rectified flow): velocity target `data − noise` worked as 0.8 − (−1.2) = 2.0, and the model learns to predict it from any point (Flow matching definition). The squared-error loss is stated only implicitly; general-path targets and x̂ conversions are not shown.

name: Timestep sampling and resolution shift for flow models (logit-normal, shift)
where: Not in the book (no logit-normal timestep sampling or resolution shift).

name: Consistency models (consistency function and training loss)
where: Ch 16 (Distillation: from 50 steps to 1): consistency models map any point on a denoising path straight to its endpoint; step distillation defined. The consistency function, loss and EMA target are not shown.

name: MeanFlow average velocity (one-step flow models)
where: Not in the book.

name: Score distillation gradients (SDS, DMD) and adversarial distillation
where: Ch 47 (3D and avatars: Route 1): DreamFusion's score distillation renders a shape from many angles and uses a 2D diffusion model's judgment to nudge it (definition); Ch 16 (Distillation) says SDXL-Turbo added a GAN-style discriminator. SDS and DMD gradients are not shown.

name: Vector quantization codebook lookup (VQ-VAE image and audio tokenizers)
where: Ch 16 (Autoregressive image generation: painting by tokens): each grid cell replaced by the closest codebook entry (Image tokenizer (VQ-VAE) definition), DALL·E 256 × 256 to 32 × 32 = 1,024 tokens from an 8,192-entry codebook; Ch 22 (Late fusion and early fusion): Vector quantization (codebook) definition. The argmin formula and bits per image are not shown.

name: VQ-VAE loss with codebook and commitment terms
where: Not in the book. Ch 16 and Ch 22 describe the codebook, but not the codebook, commitment or EMA-update terms of the VQ-VAE loss.

name: Straight-through estimator
where: Not in the book.

name: Residual vector quantization (neural audio codecs) and codec bitrate
where: Ch 22 (Hearing: how sound becomes tokens): codecs use codebooks in layers, the second encoding what the first got wrong and so on; EnCodec 75 and Mimi 12.5 frames per second; Neural audio codec definition. Ch 46 (Teaching machines to speak) mentions codec tokens. The residual recursion and bitrate formula are not shown.

name: Finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and lookup-free quantization (LFQ)
where: Not in the book (no FSQ or lookup-free quantization).

name: Gumbel-softmax (concrete) relaxation and the Gumbel-max trick
where: Not in the book.

name: Masked generative modeling and masked (discrete) diffusion
where: Ch 16 (Diffusion language models): noise means masking, the model predicts every masked position and keeps the most confident, Figure 16.11, Masked diffusion definition; Ch 16 (Self-supervised learning): BERT hides about 15% of words. MaskGIT's cosine schedule and the masked-diffusion loss are not shown.

name: InfoNCE contrastive loss
where: Ch 16 (Contrastive learning and CLIP): each row treated as a multiple-choice question, turned into percentages with softmax, penalized when the true pair does not win; Contrastive learning definitions in Ch 16, Ch 22 and Ch 27; Appendix F defines noise-contrastive estimation. The InfoNCE formula, temperature, mutual-information bound and MoCo momentum update are not shown.

name: CLIP symmetric contrastive loss with learned temperature
where: Ch 16 (Contrastive learning and CLIP): Figure 16.2 similarity matrix, softmax over rows and over columns, zero-shot classification by the closest phrase; Ch 45 (Image classification) works zero-shot picking by cosine (0.31 versus 0.27 and 0.19); Ch 16 Exercise 6. The symmetric loss formula and learned temperature are not shown.

name: SigLIP pairwise sigmoid loss
where: Ch 16 (Contrastive learning and CLIP, SigLIP definition) and Ch 22 (Step 3): each image–caption pair scored independently with a sigmoid. The loss formula, temperature and bias are not shown.

name: SimCLR NT-Xent loss (normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy)
where: Ch 45 (A quick recap: the networks that see) mentions pretraining by 'matching different crops of the same photo'; Ch 16 (Self-supervised learning) covers pretext tasks. SimCLR and NT-Xent are not named or shown.

name: Triplet loss and margin-based face-recognition losses
where: Ch 45 (Faces: Face embedding definition): photos of the same person trained to land close together and different people far apart (FaceNet, 128 numbers); Ch 46 (Speaker embedding definition) the same for voices. Triplet loss and ArcFace formulas are not shown.

name: Self-distillation without labels (DINO, BYOL-style EMA teacher)
where: Ch 45 (A quick recap: the networks that see): Meta's DINO family learned features from images alone by self-supervision ('matching different crops of the same photo'). The teacher–student self-distillation, EMA teacher and centering are not explained.

name: Masked image modeling (MAE) and joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPA)
where: Ch 16 (Self-supervised learning): masked autoencoders hide most patches and repaint them; Ch 16 (Beyond single media) and Ch 47 (Other approaches: Cosmos, World Labs and JEPA): JEPA predicts in embedding space; Ch 49 (World models) V-JEPA 2. The MAE and JEPA losses are not shown.

name: Gram-matrix style loss (neural style transfer)
where: Ch 14 (Neural style transfer bullet and definition): content from deep CNN features, style from texture statistics of its layers; Appendix F (Texture). The Gram matrix and style/content losses are not shown.

name: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and its video and audio variants
where: Ch 16 (How do you grade a generator?): FID compares statistics of features from real and generated images, lower is better (FID definition). The mean-and-covariance formula is not shown.

name: Inception Score (IS)
where: Not in the book.

name: Kernel Inception Distance and CMMD (maximum mean discrepancy)
where: Appendix F (Generative stochastic networks and moment matching): maximum mean discrepancy defined in words as comparing a rich collection of summary statistics. KID and CMMD are not named; the MMD² formula and kernels are not shown.

name: Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR)
where: Not in the book.

name: Structural similarity index (SSIM)
where: Not in the book.

name: LPIPS perceptual distance (and perceptual loss)
where: Not in the book.

name: CLIPScore (text–image alignment)
where: Ch 16 (How do you grade a generator?, CLIP score definition): similarity between image and prompt in CLIP's shared space. The w × max(cos, 0) form with w = 2.5 is not shown.

name: Pinhole camera projection, rigid transforms and stereo depth
where: Appendix F (Image formation: cameras, lenses and light): pinhole model and perspective projection, an object twice as far looks half as tall; Ch 45 (Seeing in 3D): stereo depth in words (closer objects shift more between the two images); Ch 49 (From 'go there' to motor commands): coordinate frames as 'rotate, then shift', one-degree tilt worked. Projection, rigid-transform and Z = f × B ÷ d formulas are not shown.

name: NeRF volume rendering
where: Ch 45 (Seeing in 3D, NeRF definition and Table 45.2): a network returns color and density for any point and direction, rendered by querying many points along each pixel's line of sight. The volume-rendering sum and positional encoding are not shown.

name: 3D Gaussian splatting (alpha compositing of Gaussians)
where: Ch 45 (Seeing in 3D, Gaussian splatting definition): millions of soft, colored, semi-transparent blobs; worked file size (about 60 numbers per Gaussian, 3,000,000 × 60 = 180 million numbers); Ch 47 (3D and avatars). Alpha compositing, covariance and loss formulas are not shown.

name: Object-detection box encoding and non-maximum suppression (NMS)
where: Ch 45 (How a one-stage detector works): grid cells predict boxes, NMS keeps the most confident of heavily overlapping boxes (definition, Figure 45.4); Appendix F (ResNeXt, RegNet and anchor boxes): detectors predict how to stretch and shift each anchor. Box-offset encoding and the IoU-threshold loop are not shown (IoU itself is worked in Ch 45, Scoring a detector).

name: Sampling rate, Nyquist limit and raw audio size
where: Ch 46 (Sound as numbers): Nyquist limit = half the sampling rate (16,000 samples per second captures up to 8,000 Hz); bits per second worked as 44,100 × 16 × 2 = 1,411,200; also Ch 3 (audio bitrate). Aliasing and the 6.02 dB per bit rule are not shown.

name: Discrete Fourier transform, short-time Fourier transform and the spectrogram
where: Ch 46 (Spectrograms: a picture of sound): Fourier transform definition, 25 ms windows every 10 ms, one column per window stacked into a spectrogram (Figure 46.3); Appendix F (Fast convolution) defines the FFT. The DFT/STFT formulas, bin spacing and frame count are not shown.

name: Mel scale, log-mel spectrogram and MFCCs (with the musical pitch formula)
where: Ch 46 (Spectrograms: a picture of sound): Mel scale and Log-mel spectrogram definitions, 80 mel bands, worked 100 × 80 = 8,000 numbers per second. The mel formula, MFCCs and the MIDI pitch formula are not shown.

name: Audio frame and token rates
where: Ch 46 (Spectrograms): a new window every 10 ms gives 100 columns per second; Ch 22 (Hearing: how sound becomes tokens): Whisper's 1,500 vectors per 30-second window = 50 per second, 3,600 × 32 = 115,200 tokens per hour; EnCodec 75 and Mimi 12.5 frames per second (also Ch 46, WaveNet worked example). Codec tokens per second = frame rate × codebooks is described but not computed.

name: Word error rate (WER) and character error rate (CER)
where: Ch 46 (Measuring speech recognition: word error rate): WER = (S + D + I) ÷ N, worked 3 ÷ 9 ≈ 33%, CER definition; Exercises 2, 3 and 8.

name: Connectionist temporal classification (CTC) loss
where: Not in the book. Ch 46 (The deep learning turn) describes end-to-end recognition without CTC.

name: Path cost, uniform-cost search and search-tree size
where: Ch 48 (Blind search: breadth-first and depth-first): uniform-cost search defined, most nodes sit in the deepest level, bidirectional search worked as 10^6 versus 2 × 10^3; Ch 48 (Game trees) Table 48.4 (35^80 ≈ 10^123); Ch 49 (100^7 = 10^14). The path-cost sum and the geometric tree-size formula are not written out.

name: A* search evaluation function (and greedy best-first search)
where: Ch 48 (A*: search with a sense of direction): f = g + h with Table 48.2 and the grid walk-through; greedy best-first (h alone) in words; Exercise 4; Check your understanding 2.

name: Admissible and consistent heuristics, common heuristics and effective branching factor
where: Ch 48 (A*: search with a sense of direction): admissible = never overestimates the true remaining cost; Manhattan distance worked 0 + 7 = 7; heuristics from relaxed problems (Planning with actions). Consistency, max of heuristics, straight-line distance and effective branching factor are not shown.

name: Weighted A* (bounded-suboptimal search)
where: Ch 48 (A*: search with a sense of direction): g + 2 × h, path at most the weight times the best when h is admissible; Weighted A* definition.

name: Simulated annealing acceptance rule
where: Ch 48 (Local search: improving one solution at a time): accepts worse moves with a probability that shrinks as the temperature falls (Simulated annealing definition). The exp(ΔE ÷ T) rule and cooling schedule are not shown.

name: Genetic algorithm selection, crossover and mutation
where: Ch 54 (One generation, worked by hand): roulette selection 17 ÷ 48 ≈ 35%, one-point crossover 01|110, bit-flip mutation; Exercises 5 and 6 (Colab code).

name: Minimax value of a game tree
where: Ch 48 (Minimax, worked by hand): min at O's level, max at X's level, worked tic-tac-toe tree (Figure 48.3); depth cutoff with an evaluation function in Ch 48 (Alpha-beta pruning and evaluation functions); Exercise 1.

name: Alpha–beta pruning bounds
where: Ch 48 (Alpha-beta pruning and evaluation functions): the cut shown on Option B in words, and perfect move ordering lets alpha-beta search about twice as deep. The α and β bookkeeping and the O(b^(m/2)) formula are not shown.

name: Expectiminimax (games with chance)
where: Ch 48 (Games with dice: chance nodes): probability-weighted average at chance nodes, worked 1/36 ≈ 0.03 versus 11/36 − 1/36 = 10/36 ≈ 0.28.

name: Weighted linear evaluation function
where: Ch 48 (Alpha-beta pruning and evaluation functions): evaluation function defined as scoring an unfinished position, e.g. counting material and judging king safety; Stockfish uses a small network. The weighted linear sum is not shown.

name: UCT selection rule for Monte Carlo tree search
where: Ch 48 (Monte Carlo tree search): `win rate + c × square root of (ln N ÷ n)`, worked 1.30 versus 2.06 with c = 1.4.

name: PUCT: neural-network-guided MCTS (AlphaZero, MuZero)
where: Ch 48 (AlphaGo and Move 37; AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero): a policy network suggests moves and a value network judges positions, both guiding MCTS; Figure 48.4 plays the most-visited move. The PUCT rule, visit-count policy and AlphaZero loss are not shown.

name: Constraint satisfaction problem (formal definition and counts; no single numeric equation)
where: Ch 48 (Constraint satisfaction: puzzles, timetables and schedules): variables, domains and constraints worked for four meetings, brute force 3 × 3 × 3 × 1 = 27, arc consistency and backtracking worked; Appendix F (Structure in constraint problems). AC-3 complexity is not shown.

name: Truth-table semantics, entailment and model checking
where: Ch 54 (Logic: the mathematics underneath the rules): 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 situations checked by brute force, entailment defined as true in every situation where the facts hold, IF-THEN rewritten as NOT A OR B. Full truth tables and De Morgan's laws are not shown.

name: Resolution and modus ponens inference rules
where: Ch 54 (Logic: the mathematics underneath the rules): resolution worked ('alarm OR guard' with 'NOT guard' gives 'alarm'; 'NOT alarm OR locked' with 'alarm' gives 'locked'), Resolution rule definition; modus ponens as forward chaining in Ch 54 (A tiny expert system, worked by hand). Refutation is not shown.

name: First-order logic: quantifiers, unification and generalized modus ponens
where: Ch 54 (Logic: the mathematics underneath the rules): first-order logic with 'for all' and 'there exists', the Maria insurance example; Appendix F (Unification, lifted inference and fast rule engines): unification of Mortal(x) with Mortal(Socrates). Quantifier equivalences and generalized modus ponens are not written out.

name: STRIPS/PDDL action model for classical planning
where: Ch 48 (Planning with actions: from Shakey to PDDL): actions as preconditions and effects (Table 48.3), worked tea plan, PDDL. The applicability test and RESULT(s, a) = (s − DEL) ∪ ADD are not shown.

name: Bayesian network joint factorization
where: Ch 54 (A Bayesian network, worked by hand): joint probabilities computed as products of the tables (1,000 × 0.2 × 0.3 mornings, 99% wet); parameter counts 6 versus 2^3 − 1 = 7 and 30 × 2^3 = 240 versus about a billion. The general product formula is not written symbolically.

name: Markov random fields, factor graphs and conditional random fields
where: Ch 54 (A Bayesian network, worked by hand): Markov random field and probabilistic graphical model definitions; Appendix F (Reading independence off a diagram) defines factor graphs. The clique-potential formula and CRFs are not shown.

name: Inference by enumeration (normalization constant α)
where: Ch 54 (A Bayesian network, worked by hand): P(rain given wet) = 185.4 ÷ 405.4 ≈ 0.46 by summing over the sprinkler and normalizing, plus the two explaining-away cases; Exercise 3.

name: Variable elimination and belief propagation
where: Not explained. Appendix F (Reading independence off a diagram) says only that message-passing algorithms run on factor graphs; variable elimination and the sum-product message are absent.

name: Noisy-OR conditional distribution
where: Appendix F (Noisy-OR and continuous variables): no fever with both causes 0.6 × 0.2 = 0.12, so fever 0.88; Noisy-OR definition. The leak term is not shown.

name: Approximate inference by sampling: likelihood weighting, Gibbs sampling and Metropolis–Hastings
where: Ch 54 (A Bayesian network, worked by hand): simulate 100,000 mornings, keep the wet ones and count (rejection sampling), MCMC defined; Appendix F (Gibbs sampling and importance sampling) defines both in words. Likelihood weighting and Metropolis–Hastings are not covered.

name: Causal effect by back-door adjustment (the do-operator)
where: Ch 54 (A worked confounder): adjustment worked as 0.5 × 28% + 0.5 × 8% = 18% versus 0.5 × 30% + 0.5 × 10% = 20%; Ch 54 (Pearl's ladder of causation): P(Y given do(X)); Exercise 7. The back-door criterion is not named.

name: Hidden Markov model joint probability
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time: hidden states and filters): Markov chain and HMM definitions, umbrella example with transition (0.7/0.3) and emission (0.9/0.2) probabilities; Ch 46 (HMM definition). The joint-probability product is not shown.

name: Bayes filter and the HMM forward algorithm (filtering), with the POMDP belief update
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time: hidden states and filters): umbrella filter worked, predict 0.82 × 0.7 + 0.18 × 0.3 ≈ 0.63, correct 0.567 ÷ (0.567 + 0.074) ≈ 0.88; Filtering definition. Ch 48 (Markov decision processes) describes the POMDP belief update in words. Forward-variable notation is not shown.

name: Forward–backward smoothing
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time): one sentence, smoothing revises estimates of past states using later evidence. The forward–backward formulas are not shown.

name: Viterbi algorithm (most likely hidden-state sequence)
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time): one sentence, Viterbi finds the single most likely sequence of hidden states, used by HMM speech recognizers. The recursion is not shown.

name: Baum–Welch algorithm (EM for hidden Markov models)
where: Ch 10 (Gaussian mixtures, EM paragraph and definition): EM explained and said to be how the HMMs of classic speech recognition were trained; Appendix F (The ELBO, MAP inference and wake-sleep) mentions EM. Baum–Welch is not named and its re-estimation formulas are not shown.

name: Kalman filter predict step
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time): the Kalman filter does the predict-and-correct arithmetic exactly for bell-shaped noise (Kalman filter definition); Appendix F (Optimal control: LQR, DDP and LQG; Tracking many objects at once). The predict equations are not shown.

name: Kalman filter update step (Kalman gain)
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time): the Kalman filter optimally blends a motion prediction with noisy measurements (definition). The Kalman gain and update equations, including the 1D form, are not shown.

name: Particle filter (sequential importance resampling)
where: Ch 54 (Reasoning over time, Particle filter definition): belief as thousands of particles, moved by the motion model, more copies kept of those that match the sensors. Weights, normalization, effective sample size and resampling rule are not shown.

name: Occupancy-grid log-odds update
where: Ch 50 (Perception: what is around me?, Occupancy grid definition): cells around the car with an estimate of whether each is occupied. The log-odds update is not shown.

name: Forward kinematics and transform chains
where: Ch 49 (From 'go there' to motor commands: the classic toolkit): forward and inverse kinematics defined, forward kinematics as a chain of 'rotate, then shift' steps through coordinate frames, worked one-degree camera tilt. The two-link formula, transform chain and Jacobian inverse are not shown.

name: PID controller
where: Ch 49 (From 'go there' to motor commands: Holding steady): P term 0.5 × 10 = 5, D term 0.5 × 4 = 2, net 3; integral term explained in words; PID controller definition. The integral and discrete-time formulas are not written out.

name: Model predictive control objective
where: Ch 49 (From 'go there' to motor commands): MPC plans the best commands over a short horizon with a model, applies only the first, measures and re-solves (definition); Appendix F (Optimal control: LQR, DDP and LQG). The cost function and constraints are not shown.

name: RRT extension step (sampling-based motion planning)
where: Ch 49 (Collision-free paths): RRT repeatedly picks a random pose, finds the nearest pose in the tree and steps a little toward it if the step is collision-free (definition); Appendix F (Other motion planners). The step formula and RRT* radius are not shown.

name: Expected utility and the maximum-expected-utility principle
where: Ch 48 (Deciding when you are not sure: expected utility): umbrella worked, leave it 0.7 × 100 + 0.3 × 0 = 70 versus take it 80, break-even at 20%; Maximum expected utility principle definition.

name: Value of perfect information (VPI)
where: Ch 48 (Deciding when you are not sure: expected utility): perfect forecast worth 0.3 × 80 + 0.7 × 100 = 94, so information worth 94 − 80 = 14 points; Value of information definition.

name: Utility of money, risk attitude and multiattribute utility
where: Ch 48 (Deciding when you are not sure: expected utility): risk aversion with the sure $1,000 versus a coin flip for $2,000 (definition); Appendix F (Multiattribute utility and decision networks): often a weighted sum; Appendix F (Human judgment and irrationality). Certainty equivalent, risk premium and the additive formula are not shown.

name: Value iteration and policy iteration (planning with a known MDP model)
where: Ch 48 (Markov decision processes: the formal frame): value iteration defined as 'best immediate reward plus the discounted value of where that action leads', worked sweeps C = 10, B = 0.9 × 10 = 9, A = 0.9 × 9 = 8.1; policy iteration in words. The sum over P(s′ | s, a), stopping rule and policy-iteration equations are not shown.

name: Fuzzy membership, fuzzy operators and defuzzification
where: Ch 54 (Fuzzy logic: degrees of truth): ramp memberships worked ((28 − 26) ÷ 5 = 0.4, (26 − 24) ÷ 6 ≈ 0.33), weighted-average defuzzification ≈ 67%; Exercise 4 (MAX/MIN ramp formulas). Fuzzy AND = min, OR = max, NOT = 1 − μ are not stated.
